title: Theme extraction record
description: One pass of Stage 1 over one commentary for one theme. Extraction states what a commentary says at a locatable place; it never interprets, and it never reaches past the commentary to the primary text. Every unit carries a verbatim quote so the claim can be checked mechanically.

theme.description: Theme id; must exist in synthesis/themes.json.

commentary.description: Commentary slug (filename stem); must exist in synthesis/corpus.json.

source_sha256.description: Digest of the commentary file this pass read. When the file's current digest differs, the record is stale and its quotes are no longer authoritative.

coverage.description: 'complete' asserts the whole commentary was scanned. A partial pass must say what it covered in coverage_note; the status report treats it as unfinished.

absences.description: Places the theme was expected and is not present. Absences periodize; an empty array is a claim, not a default.

id.description: theme/commentary-shortname/NNN. Stable across re-runs: reuse the id when re-extracting the same unit.

primary_locator.description: Citation into the primary text in that text's own system (SZ 126, GA 19 § 12, Hua IV § 18), as the commentary gives it. Never supplied from outside the commentary.

stratum.description: Stratum id from synthesis/chronology.json, where the commentary's own text assigns the passage to a dated layer.

term.description: The term as it appears at that place - German, Greek, or the commentary's fixed English rendering.

claim.description: One sentence: what is claimed there. Not what it means, not what it leads to.

status.description: What the term is doing at that place.

quote.description: Verbatim from the commentary, inside the located section. Checked by scripts/synthesis_validate.py; a quote that does not appear fails the build.

expected_because.description: Why the theme was expected here - the argument that would have called for it.

absent_terms.description: Terms checked for and not found. Defaults to the theme's search terms. The validator re-checks these against the section and fails if one is in fact present.
